# onpager_schedule (Resource)

Manage an OnPager schedule's settings independently of its rotations, overrides and handover settings.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "onpager_schedule" "example" {
  team_id = var.team_id
  name    = "Operations"
  enabled = true
}

variable "team_id" {
  description = "Existing active owning team UUID."
  type        = string
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Nonempty schedule name without leading or trailing whitespace. The API permits at most 200 characters.
- `team_id` (String) Owning team UUID. Changing the owner replaces the schedule. Must be a nonzero canonical lowercase UUID.

### Optional

- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the schedule is enabled. Defaults to `true`. Disabled schedules remain in state and can be re-enabled. Import and refresh do not change this setting.
- `work_calendar_id` (String) Work-calendar UUID belonging to the same team. Must be a nonzero canonical lowercase UUID when set. Omission or `null` clears the link. Referenced calendar entries must use whole-second boundaries.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Stable nonzero canonical lowercase OnPager UUID.
- `revision` (Number) Schedule settings revision used in strong numeric `If-Match` for updates and disable. Independent of rotation and override changes; stale settings report a conflict.

## Import

Import using the schedule UUID. Import reads schedule settings without
enumerating child rotations or overrides.

Use an `import` block:

```terraform
import {
  to = onpager_schedule.example
  id = "99999999-9999-4999-8999-999999999999"
}
```

Or use the CLI:

```shell
terraform import onpager_schedule.example 99999999-9999-4999-8999-999999999999
```

## Lifecycle

This resource owns schedule settings. Primary rotations, overrides and handover
notification settings are managed separately. Their revisions do not invalidate
the schedule settings revision.

Creation requires an active team and initially creates an enabled schedule. With
`enabled = false`, the provider saves the identity before disabling it. A failed
disable retains state and reports an error. Renames, calendar changes and
enabling require an active owner. Re-enabling with a retired calendar link is
rejected; clear or replace the link explicitly. Linked calendar entries must use
whole-second boundaries.

Destroy disables the schedule, including under an inactive owner, retaining its
UUID, rotations, overrides and history. Disabled schedules remain readable and
can be re-enabled.

Concurrent settings changes report a conflict and require a new plan. The
provider does not retry with a newer revision. Only confirmed absence removes
state; authorization, transport, identity and malformed-response errors retain
it.

## Permissions

Requires owning-team grants `schedules.create`, `schedules.read`,
`schedules.update` and `schedules.delete`, including for service accounts.
